Overview
The goal here is to identify additional opportunities where tgndata can drive greater impact,  whether by increasing scope (more competitors, products), activating additional modules (e.g., Promotions, Assortment, Dynamic Pricing), or expanding to new regions.
Expansion is not just a sales motion,  it’s a natural continuation of Customer Success.
CSMs are responsible for recognizing signals of untapped value and aligning those opportunities with the customer’s evolving business priorities.
Why Expansion Matters
Healthy expansion is a direct reflection of strong adoption and demonstrated ROI.

section: When customers choose to expand, it’s because tgndata has become a trusted part
text:
When customers choose to expand, it’s because tgndata has become a trusted part of their pricing or commercial decision making process. Expansion increases customer stickiness, raises lifetime value, and strengthens relationships across multiple levels of the organization.
Expansion Triggers
CSMs should continuously monitor for signals that indicate expansion readiness. Some examples are:
Usage signals: The maximum of their products’ number has been reached or is getting really close.
Business maturity: Customer starts asking “what else can we monitor?” or requests custom analyses beyond current scope.
Strategic changes: New product launches, market entries, or pricing strategy shifts that require broader data coverage.
Each trigger should prompt the CSM to initiate an exploratory discussion about how tgndata can support these evolving needs.
CSM Responsibilities During Expansion

section: Identify Expansion Paths
text:
Identify Expansion Paths
Review usage and Success Plans to spot where tgndata could deliver additional value.
Typical paths include:
Adding new products, retailers, or countries.
Activating new modules (Promotions, Dynamic Pricing, Assortment).
Extending access to new markets.
Increasing data refresh frequency or custom developments.
Validate Business Fit
Discuss with the customer what outcomes they’re targeting (e.g., faster competitor reaction time, full market coverage).
Confirm the business need before looping in Sales. The goal is to align the expansion with value, not quota.
Collaborate with Engineering and Sales
If the request is a custom development, it must be reviewed by engineers for feasibility and work hours.
Once validated, CSMs and Sales align on positioning, pricing, and timing.

section: The CSM provides context (use cases, ROI stories, adoption health) to support th
text:
The CSM provides context (use cases, ROI stories, adoption health) to support the commercial discussion.
Document and Track Expansion Opportunities
Record expansion opportunities in Salesforce.
Create a Success Plan objective for each identified opportunity.
Track progression from exploration → proposal → close.
Edit the Success Plan accordingly.
Expansion Readiness Checklist
Before suggesting an expansion, confirm:
The customer has achieved strong adoption (e.x., consistent activity).
Value has been demonstrated and acknowledged.
Data quality issues are stable or resolved.
Key stakeholders understand tgndata’s core workflows.
There’s an identifiable business problem the expansion will solve.
If any of these are missing, continue reinforcing adoption before introducing expansion discussions.
Expansion Execution
When the opportunity is validated:

section: Start with discovery. Ask what decisions the customer wants to support with addi
text:
Start with discovery. Ask what decisions the customer wants to support with additional data or modules.
Align the story to business outcomes. Link expansion directly to goals like market share visibility, promo efficiency, or price agility.
Involve the right personas. Bring in the stakeholders who will benefit most (Category Managers, Pricing Directors, or Regional Leads).
Leverage customer success stories. Share examples of other clients who expanded successfully and the outcomes they achieved.
Document everything. Update the Success Plan and CRM with expansion progress and expected impact.

Overview
The Customer Success team’s primary focus during the Adoption phase is to ensure that customers move beyond onboarding and begin using tgndata actively in their daily workflows. Adoption is the point where customers start realizing the initial value they expected from the platform like automating manual tasks, gaining visibility into competitor actions, improving pricing decisions, etc.
Customers who expand tgndata’s use across multiple teams or use cases (e.g., price monitoring, promotions tracking, assortment optimization, or dynamic pricing) experience higher ROI, stronger engagement, and long-term satisfaction.
Core Objectives
Embed tgndata into the customer’s daily routines by aligning product workflows with real business processes.

section: Validate early value by ensuring customers can independently achieve quick wins.
text:
Validate early value by ensuring customers can independently achieve quick wins.
Drive multi-user engagement across pricing, analytics, and management roles.
Track measurable adoption metrics that indicate healthy, sustained use.
Identify expansion opportunities to increase ROI and customer stickiness.
Key Adoption Activities
Usage Monitoring and InsightsCSMs should continuously monitor product usage metrics such as logins, reports created, alerts configured, and dashboards viewed. These insights help identify which users are actively engaging with tgndata and where additional support might be needed.
Customer Enablement SessionsThese include workshops and training sessions that deepen product knowledge and confidence. They should be tailored to customer maturity, data readiness, and desired outcomes.

section: Support ReachoutBy reviewing ticket themes and frequency, CSMs can spot where cu
text:
Support ReachoutBy reviewing ticket themes and frequency, CSMs can spot where customers are learning, identify recurring friction points, and use follow-ups to turn support moments into short learning opportunities that reinforce adoption.
Success Plan EngagementAssess how engaged customers are with their defined goals and actions. The Success Plan isn’t just a tracker,  it’s how the CSM ensures customers stay connected to their objectives, make visible progress, and keep momentum toward measurable outcomes.
CSM-led Enablement and Expansion
Use-Case Enablement
Enable customers on the workflows that map directly to their desired business outcomes. This involves guiding them through hands-on usage of the platform, identifying potential blockers, and ensuring they can perform key actions independently. CSMs focus on:

section: Creating quick time-to-value through guided configuration of alerts, reports, an
text:
Creating quick time-to-value through guided configuration of alerts, reports, and dashboards.
Aligning feature usage to business goals (e.g., faster reaction to competitor price changes).
Reinforcing stickiness by showing how tgndata integrates into existing routines.
Use-Case Expansion
Once the customer is comfortable with their initial workflows, CSMs can introduce new modules or use cases to drive deeper adoption (e.g., adding assortment or promo tracking after mastering price monitoring).  This motion typically starts with a discovery conversation, identifying opportunities where tgndata can solve additional pain points, followed by targeted enablement sessions to drive usage in these new areas.
All enablement and expansion activities should be reflected in the customer’s Success Plan and linked to measurable adoption objectives.
Usage Monitoring and Insights

section: Usage data becomes the clearest window into whether the customer is truly adopti
text:
Usage data becomes the clearest window into whether the customer is truly adopting tgndata. The objective is not to tick metrics, but to translate data into action: detect behavior patterns early, guide users toward habits, and ensure the platform becomes part of their daily decision-making. Of course since not of all our users use our platform this section only applies only to those who have access.
Purpose
Consistent usage across multiple users signals that tgndata is integrated into the customer’s workflow. Conversely, inactivity or one-user dependency often means the team hasn’t yet understood how to connect the tool to their business outcomes.
How CSMs Use It During Adoption
Detect activation patterns: Within the first few weeks, confirm that each key user has logged in and completed at least one workflow (report, alert, dashboard).

section: Track repeat behavior: Sustained use of the same features over time matters more
text:
Track repeat behavior: Sustained use of the same features over time matters more than volume spikes.
Spot uneven engagement: If usage is concentrated on one person or one module, plan a short enablement to broaden adoption.
Correlate with business moments: Increases in activity around promo periods are positive meaning that tgndata is influencing real decisions.
Intervene early: Any drop in usage should trigger outreach; adoption risks escalate fast if left for weeks.
CSM Mindset
Usage monitoring during adoption isn’t a reporting task — it’s a diagnostic tool. Each graph or dashboard view should lead to a concrete next step:
“Who needs extra help?” “Where is value already visible?” “What behavior should we reinforce?”

section: By the end of the adoption window, the goal is clear: consistent, recurring plat
text:
By the end of the adoption window, the goal is clear: consistent, recurring platform activity from at least two engaged users who rely on tgndata for their core pricing workflows.
Enablement Sessions
Enablement sessions are scheduled as often as needed based on customer maturity. CSMs should proactively suggest follow-up sessions if adoption metrics indicate low platform usage or if new team members join the customer’s organization.
Type of sessions
Workshops (45–1 hour): Hands-on, interactive sessions with live customer data to teach specific workflows, such as “Building custom reports” or “Monitoring competitor promotions.”
Enablement sessions (20–30 minutes): Focused on a single area, such as “Creating dynamic pricing rules” or “Configuring availability filters.”
Refresher Sessions: Targeted re-enablement for existing customers to reinforce adoption or introduce new features.

section: Each session should include a clear goal, such as completing a specific configur
text:
Each session should include a clear goal, such as completing a specific configuration or achieving a defined workflow milestone.
Currently available sessions
Below is a list of sessions.  Each session can be tailored to the customer’s maturity level, data setup, and specific use case:
Intro to tgndata
Audience: All usersGoal: Introduce tgndata’s capabilities and demonstrate how it supports pricing and market intelligence teams.Outcome: Participants understand core modules, navigation, and what data tgndata provides.
Navigating the Platform Efficiently
Audience: New users and analystsGoal: Learn how to move confidently across dashboards, tables, and filters.Outcome: Users can find insights quickly and interpret interface elements correctly.
Data Quality & Coverage Explained

section: Audience: Analysts, technical usersGoal: Understand tgndata’s crawling logic, da
text:
Audience: Analysts, technical usersGoal: Understand tgndata’s crawling logic, data refresh frequency, and matching process.Outcome: Users can interpret coverage metrics and explain data differences internally.
Competitor Monitoring Workshop
Audience: Pricing Managers, AnalystsGoal: Learn how to set up and monitor competitor price, availability, and promo data.Outcome: Customer creates their first competitor alerts and dashboards using their own data.
Report Building & Dashboard Creation
Audience: Analysts, Power UsersGoal: Teach how to create, customize, and schedule analytical reports and dashboards.Outcome: Customer builds and saves 2–3 key reports used in weekly operations.
Dynamic Pricing Rules Enablement
Audience: Pricing ManagersGoal: Configure pricing rules aligned with strategy and competitive positioning.Outcome: At least one pricing rule set up and simulated in the system.

section: Pricing Manager Strategic Enablement
text:
Pricing Manager Strategic Enablement
Audience: Pricing Managers, DirectorsGoal: Connect tgndata’s data and alerts to pricing decision frameworks.Outcome: Customer integrates tgndata insights into their pricing update processes.
Advanced Alerting & Automation
Audience: Analysts, Technical usersGoal: Set up complex alerts and automation flows to save manual work.Outcome: Customer automates key monitoring tasks.
API & Feed Integration
Audience: IT / Integrations teamsGoal: Train users on how to connect tgndata’s data to external systems.Outcome: Customer validates feed delivery and automates their reporting pipeline.
Refresher Training / Re-Enablement
Audience: Existing customers or new team membersGoal: Revisit core workflows and introduce updates.Outcome: Users regain confidence and learn about newly released features.
Expansion Workshops

section: Audience: Multi-team accountsGoal: Introduce new use cases such as dynamic prici
text:
Audience: Multi-team accountsGoal: Introduce new use cases such as dynamic pricing, assortment, or promotions monitoring.Outcome: Customer expands tgndata usage to new departments or workflows.
Internal Evangelist Training
Audience: Power users / championsGoal: Equip internal users to train their own teams using tgndata’s materials.Outcome: Customer gains independence and scales adoption internally.
Session Preparation
Before each session, the CSM should:
Review the customer’s Success Plan, adoption metrics, and relevant use cases.
Prepare a short agenda and confirm attendees (e.g., pricing team, analyst, or manager).
Identify measurable outcomes (e.g., “Customer configures 3 competitor alerts”).
Conducting the Session
Reconnect the session’s purpose to the customer’s objectives.
Use real examples from their account whenever possible.

section: Keep at least half of the time hands-on — have users perform tasks themselves.
text:
Keep at least half of the time hands-on — have users perform tasks themselves.
Pause regularly to validate understanding and answer questions.
Highlight small wins to build momentum and confidence.
After the Session
Share the deck and recording (if available).
Document progress and outcomes in the CRM or Success Plan.
Follow up on any unanswered questions or unresolved blockers.
Schedule a short follow-up check-in to validate that users have continued the workflows independently.
Identify potential expansion topics for future enablement.
Support Reachout
During the adoption window, support activity provides live evidence of engagement. Customers who reach out for help are interacting with the platform, testing workflows, and pushing boundaries which is exactly what we want.
Purpose
Healthy support reachouts show that users care enough about tgndata to ask questions and fix issues.

section: The content of those tickets tells a story:
text:
The content of those tickets tells a story:
Configuration or “how-to” requests → users are learning.
Optimization or API questions → users are expanding.
Silence → risk of disengagement.
How CSMs Use It During Adoption
Track and interpret trends: Review ticket themes weekly. Repetitive issues on the same topic signal a training gap; diverse, exploratory questions show curiosity.
Close the loop fast: Follow up on key tickets personally — “I saw your question about alerts. Want a 10-minute call to go over best practices?”
Collaborate with Support: Stay aware of which accounts generate tickets and why; this coordination lets you differentiate friction from growth.
Turn issues into learning: Convert common questions into micro-guides, FAQ updates, or quick screen-share demos.
CSM Mindset

section: Support tickets during adoption aren’t red flags, they’re breadcrumbs showing wh
text:
Support tickets during adoption aren’t red flags, they’re breadcrumbs showing where customers are engaging. The absence of tickets often means users aren’t yet deep enough in the product to hit real scenarios.
By the end of the adoption phase, an ideal customer will:
Use Support selectively and effectively.
Have transitioned from “how do I?” to “can we also?” questions.
Show confidence in resolving minor issues themselves.
Success Plan Engagement
The Success Plan is the central thread connecting the customer’s goals to their first tangible results with tgndata. During the adoption phase, it serves as a mirror of how committed and engaged the customer is in executing the actions they’ve defined together with the CSM.
Purpose

section: Adoption succeeds when customers take ownership of their goals and actively driv
text:
Adoption succeeds when customers take ownership of their goals and actively drive the actions that lead to measurable outcomes. The Success Plan helps visualize this commitment,  showing whether customers are following through on agreed steps, allocating time and resources, and validating progress against their objectives.
How CSMs Engage with the Plan During Adoption
Gauge engagement, not just progress. Look beyond completed tasks to see whether customers are proactive,  logging into tgndata, experimenting, and initiating conversations about their goals.
Highlight shared responsibility.Reinforce that adoption is a partnership: tgndata provides guidance and data quality, while the customer owns execution and follow-through on their internal workflows.

section: Use the plan to re-energize ownership.When progress stalls, revisit the plan wit
text:
Use the plan to re-energize ownership.When progress stalls, revisit the plan with the customer to refocus on why each goal matters and what internal actions are needed next.
Acknowledge achievements publicly.Celebrate when the customer meets milestones,  not just that features were used, but that they acted on the insights to improve pricing decisions.
Mindset
A strong Success Plan doesn’t just record progress, it reflects how invested the customer is in realizing value. By the end of the adoption window, the plan should clearly show both sides’ contributions: tgndata enabling, and the customer executing. The more the customer drives their own actions, the smoother the transition into the Value Realization phase will be.

The Customer Success department is part of the Sales and Marketing function who partners with our customers to deliver value and positive business outcomes throughout their journey with tgndata as also to increase the value/MRR of the customer by proposing additional services and usage.
The team can be reached in this Google Chat channel
What is a Customer Success Specialist (CSS) at tgndata?
CSMs are accountable for customer adoption, measurable outcomes, customer satisfaction, and creating true customer advocacy. We create successful customers by enabling, training, and nurturing them throughout their journey. The following areas incorporate the remit of a CSM:

section: Customer Adoption - Ensure the customer is working towards or adopting their des
text:
Customer Adoption - Ensure the customer is working towards or adopting their desired use cases to maturity. Ensure the successful onboarding of all intended users. Identify areas of adoption risk and establish mitigating plays and programs.
Delivering Positive Business Outcomes - Ensure customers are meeting and exceeding their desired business outcomes so that customers can quantify and support their investment.
Trusted Advisor - Establish “trusted advisor” relationships with the management and technical teams on the customer side to deliver a best-in-class customer experience.
Account Expansion - Lead adoption expansion beyond the customer’s desired use cases and further customer return on investment (ROI). Partner with Sales to identify expansion opportunities and ensure we realize the expansion potential of a customer account.

section: Leading Business Reviews - Review and celebrate progress towards, or achievement
text:
Leading Business Reviews - Review and celebrate progress towards, or achievement of, the customer’s desired business outcomes. Address challenges with a plan for mitigation, align on upcoming and future customer business objectives.
Mission Statement
To deliver value to all customers by engaging in a consistent, repeatable, and scalable way so that customers see the value in their investment with tgndata. The mission of the Customer Success Department is to provide these customers with experience in order to:
Accelerate initial customer value
Maximize long-term, sustainable customer value
Improve overall customer satisfaction & referenceability
Maximize the total value of the customer to tgndata
North Star Metrics
Our top-level metrics are:
Retention Rate
Growth ARR
Customer Outcomes Realized

Overview
One of the primary tools CSMs have to become a trusted advisor and assess and improve account health is the customer cadence call. This is an opportunity for the CSM and the customer team to sync on business outcomes, priorities, progress on initiatives, and concerns, and it is a great opportunity to bring in other tgndata team members that the CSM feels should be included (for example, Product to review feature requests and the roadmap).
Cadence calls are an important aspect of CSM engagement to continue to understand customer’s evolving needs, ensure tgndata is delivering value and outcomes, unblock barriers, address issues, collect feedback, nurture relationships, and ensure the customer continues to have positive experiences.
Frequency

section: Cadence calls should be ideally on a monthly basis, considering specific custome
text:
Cadence calls should be ideally on a monthly basis, considering specific customer needs and stage in customer lifecycle. Cadence calls should be captured in Salesforce.
Lifecycle of a cadence call
An effective cadence call involves more than just the call itself. There are several stages that occur before, during, and after the call.
Preparation for the call
Leading up to a cadence call, the CSM should prepare a meeting agenda. This is the foundation of an effective call, and should be collaborated on by all attendees. The agenda should be made available to everyone at least a few days in advance of the call.
Recommended details to include in the agenda include
Attendees, both from tgndata and from the customer
Advance materials or read-only items
Discussion topics (see suggested discussion topics)
Leave room for the customer to bring up unplanned topics or questions
Recap & Next Steps

section: The topics and the naming of the cadence call (when you send an invite to the cu
text:
The topics and the naming of the cadence call (when you send an invite to the customer) are also an important part of the CSM engagement. The following names for the cadence call are recommended - ordered by popularity:
“tgndata / <CUSTOMER_NAME> CSM Call”
“tgndata -Monthly Collaboration” (Adapt, depending on the frequency)
“tgndata - CSM Call”
By developing an agenda and doing advance preparation for the meeting, the CSM will be ready with relevant questions and information for the customer.
Prep for ongoing cadence calls
After the initial call, you will have subsequent cadence calls, each of which you will need to prep for and ensure is an impactful and successful meeting.
Prior to the call, review the following items:
Success plan objectives and progress
Last timeline entry/notes doc to ensure follow-up items were closed out and if not, follow up on them during the next call

section: Renewal date to be aware of upcoming renewal
text:
Renewal date to be aware of upcoming renewal
Service utilization - if it is lower and the customer is in the second half of their annual contract, discuss the trends around this and expected behavior
Use case scoring, identifying areas where the customer is not green - discuss one or two on the call and include the value of adoption these areas and suggest enablement opportunities
With every customer call, always be sure to have an agenda prepared and share it with the customer in advance. Here is a template that you can use to prepare agendas for customer meetings.
Additionally, there may be specific items that are worthwhile to discuss about on a regular basis like:
Discuss any new needs they might have
Inform customer about our new product releases and ask for feedback
Conducting the call

section: If the CSM has sufficiently prepared, the call itself should be a comfortable an
text:
If the CSM has sufficiently prepared, the call itself should be a comfortable and valuable experience for everyone involved. The CSM should be prepared to conduct the meeting according to the agenda and cover all of the listed discussion points. This is our chance to help the customer make forward progress on their objectives by sharing our expertise and answering their questions!
The CSM should drive the call proactively so the customer sees a value in it and comes away feeling they have gotten something out of it. Try to ask questions to get into discussions and let the customer talk most of the time. When putting together the call agenda, ensure that you are covering topics that help you with your customer strategy, but also ask yourself “if I were the customer, would I find this relevant?”
Here are a few tips for having a strong cadence call:

section: Be engaged. The CSM is leading this call, and it’s important to follow what is b
text:
Be engaged. The CSM is leading this call, and it’s important to follow what is being discussed and keep the conversation moving to make the most of the allotted time. The CSM should be guiding the discussion, and taking notes.
Be flexible. Having an agenda is crucial to a well-run cadence call, but it’s equally important to be ready to go off-script. If the customer has something urgent that they need to discuss, or the conversation goes on a tangent that may yield good information, don’t try to force it back to the prepared agenda. Address the customer concerns, embrace new information with relevant questions, and anything on the agenda that isn’t critical can be delayed until the next cadence call.

section: Be responsive. No matter how much the CSM prepares for the call, the customer ca
text:
Be responsive. No matter how much the CSM prepares for the call, the customer can still throw a curveball. If they ask for information nobody on the call knows, be honest and acknowledge that, but make a plan to get that information and follow up. If you think you can answer the question, make an effort but still assure the customer you will verify what the best answer is. Do your best in the moment, and follow up on everything else in a timely manner.
Before you end the call, take a few minutes to summarize the highlights of what was discussed, and review the action items and who is responsible for each of them. It’s also worth reminding everyone of when the next cadence call is.
After the call

section: If there are no action items or follow-ups that come from a cadence call, the ca
text:
If there are no action items or follow-ups that come from a cadence call, the call was not effective. At minimum, the CSM should send a follow-up email or create a follow-up issue for the participants covering the summary information that was discussed at the end of the call, answer any questions that were posed during the call, and make sure everyone knows what the action items from the call were.
Review and update account details
After a call, there are a few items to review and update to ensure the content from the call isn’t lost and you maintain a positive relationship with the customer.
Log the Timeline entry in Salesforce
Update health score
Update Success Plan as needed
Follow up on any action items (questions, feature requests, escalations, etc.)
Send a follow up to the customer

section: It’s a good idea to start creating the agenda for the next cadence call at this
text:
It’s a good idea to start creating the agenda for the next cadence call at this point, while the call that just ended is fresh in mind.
Follow up
When crafting your follow up messages to customers, follow the below recommended guidelines to ensure a positive experience.
Strive to send your follow up email or open the follow up issue as soon as possible, or within one business day of your call. If it will take longer than that, set expectations with your customers upfront and keep them posted on progress (even if there isn’t any).
Address every action item, and if you don’t have an update yet, let them know that you’re working on it and an estimated turnaround time.
Keep your email/issue as succinct as possible, as customers probably don’t want to read lengthy emails.
Share links whenever possible, however:

section: Try to include the full link and not hyperlink on words, so that the customer kn
text:
Try to include the full link and not hyperlink on words, so that the customer knows what they’re about to click on.
Include a short summary of what the link contains so they understand why it’s valuable to them before they click on it.
Make sure you add these emails to Salesforce.
Cadence Call Notes
All customer call notes should be saved in Google Drive, following this format: /Documentations/Customer Success/Customers/Acme/Acme - Meeting Notes. For customers who have lengthy notes doc, such as those who have been customers for several years, it is recommended to break out their notes into separate docs for each FY inside of their customer folder. When doing so, add the FY to the doc titles, for example /Customers/Acme/Acme - Meeting Notes - FYXX and link all previous years’ docs at the top of the current notes doc for easy access.

section: The rationale for saving call notes in this manner is as follows:
text:
The rationale for saving call notes in this manner is as follows:
The naming convention “"Customer - Meeting Notes” allows for fast searching using Google Cloud Search for Work
Call notes frequently contain sensitive information and are for the internal team and management to review and should be kept in a place everyone who might need access can find them.
A folder structure allows non-Customer Success executives and support staff to easily locate the notes in the case of an escalation.
Call notes are tightly linked to the health score and should be available for reference in the same location as the health scorecard in Gainsight.
Access to Salesforce is limited, so other members will look for notes in Google Drive.
Customer call notes should also always be linked in Salesforce’s Account Object.

section: When CSMs are logging calls in Salesforce Timeline, they need to copy & paste th
text:
When CSMs are logging calls in Salesforce Timeline, they need to copy & paste the link to the Google Doc. They should either write a simple summary of the meeting along with the link, or have the link be a direct deep link to the date the call happened, so as to not duplicate efforts.
At the end of each customer call any changes to customer health should be reflected in the customer’s Salesforce account.
Cadence Call Topics
The below non-exhaustive list is simply suggestions for cadence calls, and other topics may be more important, so use the suggestions at your discretion.
Follow up on previously discussed items
Questions about their strategic and business outcomes and review of progress
Periodically (a couple times per year) ask about new goals or objectives they have coming up
Review upcoming features and releases
Questions relating to Adoption

section: Discovery questions about their usage, best practices, typical workflows, etc.
text:
Discovery questions about their usage, best practices, typical workflows, etc.
Learn about the customer’s preferred product areas by asking what they are mainly using in terms of features, integrations, etc., in order to know what to highlight from new releases
Discuss if there are any areas for user enablement or training
Questions about how they are leveraging other tools or integrations
Updates on customer requested features
Discuss if their users have any feedback, pain points, or blockers
Ask if there is anything the CSM can assist on towards resolution (feature requests, support tickets, etc.)

CSM Responsibilities
The CSM is responsible for coordinating with all relevant parties to develop a plan to address account risks. Typically, this will involve the sales team, as well as other relevant stakeholders such as Product Managers, marketing, executive, or engineering team members to develop and deliver the plan to address the risks. The CSM then drives execution of the strategy and is responsible for logging regular updates. When the risks have been addressed bringing the customer to a healthy / green status, the account team can agree to move the account out of the risk state.
Tracking Customer Health
CSMs can use Red, Yellow, and Green to reflect their sentiment of a customer’s health. Below is an explanation about how to think about a customer’s health.
Green

section: Customers are very likely to renew and/or expand with no known or assumed risk o
text:
Customers are very likely to renew and/or expand with no known or assumed risk of downsell or churn. Customer experience: engagement, adoption and experiences are as expected or better than expected, delivering value and outcomes as appropriate the customer’s stage in their journey. Examples:
Progressive adoption of tgndata use cases as defined by their success plan, considering their stage in their journey
Alignment with stakeholders who can drive desired outcomes
Regular communication and engagement in meetings
Positive feedback on the product and experience and/or high scores on NPS surveys
Leveraging support services as defined by creation of tickets (1-5 tickets per month)
No critical service issues
Regular usage of the platform if access is available
Yellow

section: Potential risk or significant lack of information leading to uncertainty. Indica
text:
Potential risk or significant lack of information leading to uncertainty. Indicates challenges to overcome, with a lower risk of churn or downsell. Customer’s experience: engagement, adoption and/or experiences are lower than expected, risking tgndata’s ability to deliver customer value and outcomes and/or drive future revenue growth. Examples:
Slow, delayed, or blocked adoption of tgndata use cases in support of the customer’s success plan
Customer lacks definition of goals or success criteria
High number of support cases, critical / blocker product issue(s), or poor experience based on the customer’s expectations
Lack of engagement, responsiveness or participation in meetings and/or events
Poor experiences with Support, or another part of tgndata
Working with a single contact at a company (single-threaded).

section: There might be well understood reasons within the account team why a customer is
text:
There might be well understood reasons within the account team why a customer is flagged as Yellow within the current phase of the customer lifecycle. If the CSM decides that corrective actions and follow up from team members outside of the CSM group is required the CSM must create a Jira Issue.
Red
Specific, known risks to account retention or upcoming opportunity, or overwhelming lack of information, such as unresponsiveness leading up to renewal. Customer experience: engagement, adoption and/or experiences are significantly lower than expected where issues are blocking tgndata’s ability to deliver expected value, outcomes, or positive experiences as defined by the customer. Examples:
Potential risk of contraction or churn (even if this is unconfirmed)
Lack of alignment with stakeholders who can drive outcomes

section: Product does not deliver expected value or outcomes as defined by success plan
text:
Product does not deliver expected value or outcomes as defined by success plan
No or low product adoption with no progression
Communication of poor sentiment
Lack of any engagement
Significantly poor experiences with Support or other dpt
Significant number of support tickets (16+ per month)
Reporting and Viewing Customer Health
Use the Customer Health report to view the health for your customers in one single view.
Salesforce Responsibilities
CSMs are responsible for keeping Salesforce up to date regarding all of their account risks.
At Risk Timeline Entries
For any account that is Red or Yellow, the following steps for an At Risk timeline update is required:
In the account timeline, log a Health Update, marking CSM Sentiment as Red (or Yellow).
Customer Health Conclusion:
Customer is won back:
Log Account-level Timeline Health Update type for CSM Sentiment as Green and final notes

section: Customer is lost:
text:
Customer is lost:
Log Account-level Timeline Health Update type with final update
Customer Health Update Format
The Health Update description should follow the format below. When logging the activity in Salesforce, please follow the below structure in the notes area.
What’s at risk today? - 1-2 sentences describing the specific churn risk and key metrics/data points.
What’s the mitigation plan for risk? - 1-2 sentences outlining the key actions being taken to address the risk.
What’s the timeline of the next step? - [Specific date - MM/DD/YYYY]
Here is a sample health update:
Risk: Utilization dropped to 35% with only 2 of 5 users actively using the platform. Primary champion announced departure effective end of month.
Mitigation: Scheduling executive alignment call next week to identify new champion and launching targeted training for underutilized users.
Next Step Timeline: 06/15/2025

section: This format is to satisfy a few requirements:
text:
This format is to satisfy a few requirements:
Clarity of situation and action up front (leading with key details)
Ensure the most pertinent information is readily visible in other systems where it is synced and displayed
Consistency to improve async processes
Health Update for Resolution of Risk
When a customer’s risk has been mitigated and they are no longer at risk, the CSM creates a Health Update timeline entry communicating:
The customer is no longer at risk
Key details about what mitigated the risk
What comes next
CSM Sentiment updated to reflect current health status
This is to ensure that everyone is aware of the latest details, and that we affirmatively communicate risk resolution across our systems and teams.
Here is a sample entry for risk resolution:

section: CUSTOMER X is no longer at risk. We resolved their Y challenges through engageme
text:
CUSTOMER X is no longer at risk. We resolved their Y challenges through engagement with Support, and they are now satisfied with the data. We are now focused on Z, in line with the agreed-upon success plan.
When to open an Account Escalation
If a CSM has marked an account as Red and further assistance from Product, Support or Managers+ is needed, open a Jira Issue.
Risk impact definitions
Customer Churn - fully churn the account
Tier Downgrade - move down tiers
Customer Sentiment (Impact Unknown) - customer is unhappy and the impact isn’t quantified
Competitor - any competitive intelligence we might be up against
Risk reason examples
Lack of adoption
Customer never adopted the product or specific features so they did not get value. This can be because of organizational silos or lack of internal resources.
Product Value / Gaps

section: Customer used the product and features, but did not see the value. The product d
text:
Customer used the product and features, but did not see the value. The product did not meet the requirements of the customer.
Product Quality / Availability
Customer used the product and features though they did not meet the customer’s needs or expectations. This can be defects, poor performance, or uptime/availability issues.
Lack of Engagement / Sponsor
We lost or were never able to get engagement with the customer team. The champion / sponsor left, changed responsibility, or became unresponsive. We were never able to re-establish connection with a new sponsor or champion
Loss of Budget
The prospect or customer lost budget due to business contraction, change of priorities, reduction of employees, or other. This was not a competitive loss.
Mitigation Strategies
For CSM guidance on mitigating risk, please see the Risk Types, Discovery & Mitigation Strategies page.

Overview
The customer onboarding phase is critical to getting a customer started on a successful journey with tgndata. This is our opportunity to ensure the customer achieves value and success from the start of their tgndata usage.
Onboarding steps
The onboarding process should begin when the customer opportunity reaches the end of the negotiating stage  in order to introduce the CSM while we have high-touch engagement. Once an opportunity reaches the won stage,  the Sales Director will assign the customer to a CSM in Salesforce. The assigned CSM should then start the onboarding process with the rest of the account team.
⚠️ NOTE: Please review the time to value metrics for target completion timeline.
Internal transition

section: The first step is completing the handoff from pre-sales to post-sales. This will
text:
The first step is completing the handoff from pre-sales to post-sales. This will ensure the entire account team is clear on the customer’s status, and the CSM can be properly introduced to the customer. This sync on the background of the account is essential and must happen before the CSM is on a call with the customer, so the CSM has the full background and the account team approaches the call as a united front, already understanding the customer goals and working towards achieving them.
CSS intro email and onboarding
The assigned CSM is responsible to send the introduction email outlining what a CSM does and next steps, followed by the onboarding enablement emails for all CSM assigned customers. This email will come from the assigned CSM’s email address, and should be personalized. Customers have the option to reply directly to the email and schedule a call or ask questions.

section: These emails will be sent to any customer contacts who are labeled as a Contact
text:
These emails will be sent to any customer contacts who are labeled as a Contact Person in Salesforce and at least one contact should have been labeled as part of the pre-sales process. It is recommended to label multiple contacts if possible as a Contact Person so they receive the emails as well, ensuring the enablement content is received.
Review email copy here.
Kickoff call
⏰ Target time: within 5 days of customer start date
The kickoff call is the first conversation between the CSM and the customer. This is when the CSM describes their role to the customer, and starts their own discovery process to fill in details they don’t have from the internal transition in order to start an effective engagement and create a success plan.
The goal of the kickoff call is to align on desired business outcomes, key upcoming milestones, and create clarity on our partnership as CSMs.

section: Which deck should I use for the Kickoff call?
text:
Which deck should I use for the Kickoff call?
CSMs can use this kickoff slide deck template for their kick off call.
The CSM should review and revise this deck in advance of the kickoff call based on what they already know about the customer and what they are still looking to understand.
What should I know coming out of the Kickoff call?
Ideally, the following information has been collected in the presales process and we use the kickoff to confirm and build upon this knowledge. In the times that these questions are not known, we always seek to leave the kickoff with an understanding of the following?

section: Why did you buy tgndata? Ideally you’ve already answered this question in your h
text:
Why did you buy tgndata? Ideally you’ve already answered this question in your handoff from pre-sales, so if that’s the case, reframe the question to validate that you understand they purchased tgndata for X reason and confirm your understanding of what challenges the customer is looking to solve.
What other tools are you using? Understanding what the tool landscape is for the customer is crucial in being able to help them adopt tgndata in relation to their desired use cases.
What are your business goals? What are they trying to achieve and their immediate goal of whatever they want to use tgndata for?
Are there other stakeholders to involve? Is there anyone else who would benefit from having business discussions with tgndata? CSMs should always have at least 2 regular contacts they speak with.

section: In addition to the above questions, make sure to review the tasklist for the fir
text:
In addition to the above questions, make sure to review the tasklist for the first cadence call to ensure you cover additional important items, such as support and training. One of the most important action items coming out of the kickoff call is establishing the cadence call. The CSM should have the ongoing cadence call schedule determined with the customer by the end of the kickoff call.
Success plan development (document key attributes)
Once the kickoff call is complete, the CSM should have sufficient information to start developing the success plan. This is a critical step in successful onboarding and long-term customer engagement.
⚠️ NOTE: While the CSM should be able to create an effective first iteration of the success plan at this point in onboarding, the success plan is a living document, so the CSM should continue iterating the success plan throughout the customer lifecycle.

section: Account setup
text:
Account setup
⏰ Target time: Within 25 business days from contract deal
This step ensures that the customer’s account is configured properly according to their agreed scope and requirements, allowing them to start using the service without friction. The completion of this stage marks the transition from internal setup to active customer engagement. Once complete, confirm that the account is ready for customer access.
By accomplishing the following tasks, you’ll know the account setup is completed:
Create the customer’s instance/account in our platform
Configure settings, integrations, and permissions according to the sales agreement or initial requirements
Load any initial data provided by the customer
Set up user accounts for key stakeholders
Perform initial testing to ensure functionality
Account delivery
⏰ Target time: Agreed day with customer based on setup

section: This stage marks the moment when the customer gains live access to their account
text:
This stage marks the moment when the customer gains live access to their account. The completion of this step ensures that the customer can log in successfully and is oriented on what to expect next in their onboarding journey.
By accomplishing the following tasks, you’ll know you have completed account delivery:
Send emails with login credentials and links to relevant resources (e.g., support portal, knowledge base, onboarding guides)
Confirm successful login and initial access with the customer
Briefly highlight what they should expect next (e.g., upcoming Platform training session)
Platform training
⏰ Target time: Within 7 days of customer account setup

section: The training call is the first hands-on session between the CSM and the customer
text:
The training call is the first hands-on session between the CSM and the customer. This is when the CSM demonstrates how tgndata works in practice, guiding the customer through the core workflows that align with their agreed goals. The purpose of the training call is to build user confidence, ensure the customer can start using tgndata independently, and set the foundation for adoption and value realization.
Which deck should I use for the Training call?
CSMs can use this training slide deck template for their kick off call.
The CSM should review and revise this deck in advance of the training call, tailoring examples and workflows to the customer’s agreed priorities and expected use cases.
What should I know coming out of the Training call?

section: The training call is where we move from why the customer bought tgndata to how t
text:
The training call is where we move from why the customer bought tgndata to how they will use it. By the end of the call, the CSM should be confident that:
The customer has seen the core workflows most relevant to their use cases (e.g., building reports, setting up monitoring rules, navigating analytics dashboards).
The customer understands how these workflows map directly to their stated business goals.
The main platform users are identified and have gained hands-on experience during the session.
Any knowledge gaps or additional training needs have been noted and a plan exists to address them (follow-up sessions, resources, recordings).
Next steps are clear, including immediate actions the customer should take on the platform and when the CSM will check back in.
1st Cadence Call: Future Growth Discussion & Checklist
⏰ Target time: Within 30 days of customer training

section: The first cadence call is typically the CSM’s second conversation with the custo
text:
The first cadence call is typically the CSM’s second conversation with the customer and when we start to deliver value through our efforts as a trusted advisor.
The completion of this second customer call marks the completion of customer onboarding, as we have collected all information needed and given the customer the tools they need to be successful going forward.
Once onboarding is complete, close the onboarding CTA and then move the customer into the Adoption phase of the customer lifecycle in Salesforce.
By accomplishing the following tasks, you’ll know you have completed onboarding:
Complete internal handoff, where CSM reviews the command plan, adoption goals, priorities, and stakeholders with sales
Assign tgndata Admin and/or other persona roles to primary contacts
Complete kickoff call, where the CSM:
Leads introductions
Validates the customer’s reason for purchase

section: Asks about any additional goals the customer has
text:
Asks about any additional goals the customer has
Asks about the customer’s toolstack
Asks about any additional customer stakeholders
Advises the customer on how to get support
Raises the awareness at the customer that they bookmark our page for platform/service changes and announcements (https://tgndata.com/releases-notes)
Complete initial draft of success plan, with the objective being their primary use case
Complete customer training
Complete second call (first cadence), where the CSM:
Discusses how they will work with the customer towards their goals, collecting metrics for success, milestones/timelines, and establishing next steps
Discusses the next calls cadence for communication
Complete filling out any relevant fields in Salesforce
Time to Value Metrics

section: The Time to Value KPIs are developed to help us understand key facts about how w
text:
The Time to Value KPIs are developed to help us understand key facts about how we are serving our customers, and how we could improve. Below are the processes for how CSMs should update and track their Time to Value KPIs. For definitions, please see Time to Value KPIs.
Time to Engage
Goal: 5 days
Required CSM action: log the first Timeline entry (Call or Meeting)
How is it calculated: Time to Engage is the number of days between the contract signup Start Date and the date of the first Timeline call or meeting entry. Time to Engage Calculation = Timeline call or meeting entry Date - contract Start Date. Example: If the contract Start Date is 2020-01-01 and the first call was 2020-01-12, then the Time to Engage would be 11 days.

section: Why is this metric important? Helps determine the time it takes to first engagem
text:
Why is this metric important? Helps determine the time it takes to first engagement with the customer. Engagement is defined as the first CSM meeting with the customer.
Time to First Value
Goal: 45 days
Required CSM action: Confirm users’ logins are registered in Posthog, if not, contact PM /  log the first value as an event in Saleforce
How is it calculated: Time to First Value is calculated by taking the Original Contract Date and subtracting First Value Date, which is the first users’ login to the platform after the training.
Why is this metric important? Allows visibility into customer usage of tgndata. Customers are considered to have met first value when at least 10% of their Production licenses are activated.
Time to Onboard
Goal: 45 days
Required CSM action: Close the Onboarding CTA

section: How is it calculated: Time to Onboard is the difference between contract  Start
text:
How is it calculated: Time to Onboard is the difference between contract  Start Date and the date the Onboarding CTA is closed. For example, the Onboarding CTA Start Date is 2020-08-15 and the Onboarding CTA was closed on 2020-09-18, the Time to Onboard would be 34 days.
Why is this metric important? Helps determine the length of time it took to complete all of the onboarding tasks associated with a customer.

Overview
A key part of the customer relationship lifecycle is the renewal phase. CSMs must proactively track the renewal dates of their customers and align with Sales to ensure that a customer renewal takes place.
Timeframe
3 months before the renewal date for a customer, a CTA will trigger in Salesforce to prompt the CSM to reach out to their aligned account team to discuss strategy and next steps for the renewal. The expectation is that the team will meet internally and speak with the customer regarding the renewal within the following 30 days. This leaves two months to execute any renewal strategy.
Renewal playbook steps
Renewal Review: Internal sync with sales
‘Soft’ renewal question asked by CSM
Update CSM Sentiment as appropriate

section: Once the above tasks are complete, the playbook and CTA can be closed out as all
text:
Once the above tasks are complete, the playbook and CTA can be closed out as all actionable items have been performed.
Renewal review meeting - internal sync
A renewal review meeting should have the following attendees:
Sales Director
Customer Success Manager
Soft renewal question
The CSM will ask the initial renewal question, this should be a ‘soft’ question to see if there is any risk in the account and to provide time to mitigate any risk. An example of this soft question is, “I know you have your renewal coming up in the next few months - how are you feeling about the renewal currently, and are there any changes you are considering that we can prepare for?”
If the customer indicates any risk of contraction or churn in this conversation, the CSM sets the CSM Sentiment to red, which then overrides the ‘Overall Health’ field to red also.

section: It’s important that the CSM asks this question no later than the 30-day window f
text: It’s important that the CSM asks this question no later than the 30-day window from when the CTA is automatically opened. If risk is indicated, 2 months can be enough time remaining to make a meaningful change to outcomes

Overview
An Executive Business Review (EBR) is a strategic partnership meeting where key stakeholders from both organizations assess progress and align on future priorities. Going beyond standard metrics, these sessions focus on measurable business outcomes and return on investment, ensuring the partnership continues to deliver meaningful value. The EBR creates a focused environment for customer leadership to share their evolving business objectives while collaboratively developing action plans to achieve them. This approach ensures resources and initiatives remain aligned with what matters most to the customer’s success.
Strategic Alignment with Stakeholders: The Importance of the EBR

section: The Executive Business Review brings together leadership teams to strengthen col
text:
The Executive Business Review brings together leadership teams to strengthen collaboration and drive measurable outcomes. These strategic sessions work best when key decision-makers from both organizations actively participate and share insights. Since coordinating executive schedules requires advance planning, begin preparations at least three months ahead. After initial discussions, distribute a brief summary that outlines the session’s objectives and logistics. This ensures all participants understand the purpose and can prepare meaningfully for the discussion.
Executive Business Review Process and Overview

section: This section outlines the EBR process, highlighting key stages: preparation, del
text:
This section outlines the EBR process, highlighting key stages: preparation, delivery, and follow-ups. While the process can be tailored to meet specific customer needs, this guide provides a typical flow to ensure strategic alignment, seamless execution, and timely action on key outcomes.
Internal Alignment (3-4 months prior): CSM and the account team set goals, timing, and participants to ensure a successful EBR.
Initial Customer Discussion (3 months prior): CSM engages with the customer to define focus areas and align attendees.
Scheduling (2-3 months prior): Confirm date and attendees, and secure participation from tgndata leadership if needed..
EBR Planning (1 month prior): Build the EBR content, aligning with internal and customer stakeholders to ensure strategic focus.

section: Internal Review (3-4 weeks prior): Finalize the presentation with internal tgnda
text:
Internal Review (3-4 weeks prior): Finalize the presentation with internal tgndata teams and adjust based on feedback.
Customer Review (2-3 weeks prior): Validate the agenda and content with the customer to ensure alignment with their expectations.
Delivery: The EBR is conducted, focusing on strategic alignment and driving outcomes for the customer.
Follow-ups (Within 1 business day): A follow-up email is sent to review action items, ensuring timely completion. The Success Plan is also updated to reflect insights from the EBR.
Final Review with the Customer

section: Throughout the EBR’s development, the CSM & account team collaborate with their
text:
Throughout the EBR’s development, the CSM & account team collaborate with their customer contacts. A final review of the EBR is conducted with the account team and customer contacts to ensure content & talk track align with expectations and are properly structured. Proactive communication is coordinated to keep the EBR planning on track and include all necessary participants.
Sample Agenda: Reviewing ROI, Impact Analysis, and Future Goals
The EBR session focuses on evaluating the customer’s tgndata adoption ROI, its impact on their business, and alignment on future goals. It provides an opportunity to review progress, address challenges, and plan next steps to ensure ongoing value and strategic alignment.
Sample Agenda:
Welcome and Introductions – Overview of key attendees and meeting objectives.
Customer Journey – Overview of the reason for purchase and tgndata enablement journey.

section: ROI & Value Review – Assess the measurable impact of tgndata solutions on busine
text:
ROI & Value Review – Assess the measurable impact of tgndata solutions on business outcomes.
Adoption & Success Metrics – Review current adoption progress and identify areas for improvement.
Future Goals & Roadmap Alignment – Discuss upcoming initiatives, long-term goals, and how tgndata can support them.
Action Items and Next Steps – Confirm key takeaways and follow-up actions to drive future success.
Additional Conversation Points
These questions facilitate discussion and help uncover key business objectives:
What are your largest current commercial or pricing initiatives this year?
Looking ahead, what are your top 2-3 priorities for the coming year?
What significant changes have occurred in your market or internal strategy since last year (new competitors, categories, pricing model shifts)?

section: Where do you see your pricing or eCommerce organization evolving in the next few
text:
Where do you see your pricing or eCommerce organization evolving in the next few years? What are your long-term goals?
Regarding pricing and competitor monitoring, how does your team currently manage analysis and response? Who is involved, and how quickly can decisions be made?
How are competitor actions or market fluctuations affecting your pricing processes and timelines today?
EBR Length
The recommended EBR length is typically 90 minutes; however, this is flexible based on customer needs and content. An EBR should provide time for key focus areas and customer objectives, ensuring maximum benefit to all involved.
FAQ
Q: Is this EBR just another sales pitch for renewal? A: No, it is not. The EBR is a strategic touchpoint focused on aligning tgndata with the customer’s organizational objectives, not a renewal conversation. Renewal discussions are separate and follow a different process.

section: Q: Who should attend the EBR from the customer side? A: Key stakeholders who inf
text:
Q: Who should attend the EBR from the customer side? A: Key stakeholders who influence or oversee strategic initiatives should attend, ensuring the session aligns tgndata solutions with long-term objectives.
Q: How is an EBR different from regular cadence calls? A: Cadence calls are often project-focused, whereas an EBR provides a strategic review of long-term goals, current successes, and future roadmaps, involving leadership from both sides.
Q: How are feature requests handled during the EBR? A: The EBR focuses on strategic goals, but notable feature requests aligning with objectives may be acknowledged. In-depth feature discussions are usually handled separately.
Q: What kind of preparation should a customer do before the EBR? A: Reviewing tgndata usage and identifying upcoming initiatives or goals helps ensure a productive discussion on how tgndata can best support objectives.

text: Now that the account is in post-sales, the CSM takes primary responsibility for guidance & best practices conversations, customer enablement, and product usage. Most responsibilities of sales will transition to the CSM at this point.

Types of Risk
These as the most common types of risk in an account:
Cost/Budget
Over License
Acquisition by larger entity
Downsizing
ROI (the customer doesn’t feel they’re getting value)
Not a priority
Lack of a plan
Lack of leadership support
Competitive
Product (the product does do what they want or meets their needs or isn’t mature enough)
Lack of Engagement/Loss of Champion
Discovery into the Risk
Based on the identified type of risk, the CSM can use some of the following questions to dig a bit deeper into the risk, that may help identify mitigation options:
Cost/Budget
Over License
Do you know how to regularly prune monitored products/websites users?
Are you aware of our other plans?
Acquisition by larger entity
What is the integration plan and timeline with the new entity?

doc: Strategies for Mitigating Risk In Customer Accounts
section: Will you be required to adopt their toolchain?
text:

What tools does the new entity use?

ROI (the customer doesn’t feel they’re getting value)
Not a priority / Lack of leadership support
What are your pricing priorities? How can we align with those?
Lack of a plan
How can we help you adopt greater use and derive greater value from tgndata?
Where do you feel you're getting the most value out of tgndata right now?

Competitive

Product (the product does not do what they want or meets their needs or isn’t mature enough)

section: Have you worked with your CSM on a prioritized list of features?
text:
Have you worked with your CSM on a prioritized list of features?
What feature(s) do you need **right now** to continue using tgndata?
Lack of Engagement/Loss of Champion

Mitigation
Once we know the risk and done some discovery into that risk, we have some options available to help mitigate that risk:
Cost/Budget
Show cost efficiency vs. alternatives: Demonstrate that tgndata consolidates multiple needs (price monitoring, assortment tracking, promotions analysis) into one source of truth — often replacing several partial tools or manual efforts.
Highlight operational savings: Quantify the hours saved by automating data collection and reporting.

doc: Strategies for Mitigating Risk In Customer Accounts
section: Position as cost avoidance: Emphasize how missing or delayed pricing data leads
text:
Position as cost avoidance: Emphasize how missing or delayed pricing data leads to revenue leakage or margin loss, far outweighing the subscription cost.
Offer tier flexibility: When needed, propose temporary scaling down in monitored scope or feature access to keep continuity and prevent churn.
ROI
Reinforce ROI narratives: Use recent case studies or success metrics (e.g., “Customers typically identify 3–5% pricing misalignments in their first 90 days”).
Build a personalized ROI summary: CSMs can use account data (alerts, reports, decisions made) to show how tgndata has already delivered measurable savings or competitive advantage.
Collaborate with Product Marketing: Use visual or executive-ready ROI slides that link customer goals to achieved outcomes (faster reaction time, improved price index, better promo planning).

text:
Revisit Success Plan outcomes: Tie daily activities back to original goals and show visible progress.  Adoption alone is not enough if outcomes aren’t recognized.
Competitive
Understand the “why,” not just the “who.” Is the competitor cheaper, faster, or pitching a specific feature gap? Address that directly rather than comparing logos.
Leverage Product Marketing resources: Use internal battle cards or comparison sheets highlighting tgndata’s strengths (data accuracy, custom matching, flexible integrations, and deep market coverage).
Validate data quality differences: Offer to benchmark specific categories or shops head-to-head.
Reinforce partnership value: Emphasize responsiveness, customization, and reliability — areas where internal tools or smaller vendors often fail.

Identify the exact gap: Through discovery, determine if the issue is about functionality, data coverage, or usability.
Differentiate between maturity and feature gap: If the customer isn’t aware of existing capabilities, schedule a targeted enablement session.
Engage Product or Data teams when needed: Offer roadmap visibility or connect the customer directly with a Product Manager for transparency and feedback.
Product Usage (not using features & functionality in their license plan)
Offer workflow-specific workshops: Show how to activate underused features (e.g., setting up assortment coverage alerts, or leveraging historical trends).
Connect unused modules to business goals: For example, if the customer wants margin protection, show how promo tracking or availability monitoring contributes to that goal

section: Highlight missed opportunities: Use data comparisons to illustrate what insights
text:
Highlight missed opportunities: Use data comparisons to illustrate what insights they’re currently not leveraging (e.g., “Your competitors ran 15 promotions you didn’t see last quarter”).
Lack of engagement/Loss of champion
For low engagement:
Revisit communication rhythm — check if cadence or format needs adjustment.
Share short, tangible insights from their own data to re-spark interest (“This week your average price gap with X retailer closed by 4%”).
Offer quick success recaps to remind them of achieved value.
For loss of champion:
Work with Sales to identify the replacement early and onboard them fast with a condensed training + success summary.
Find active users who already value tgndata and elevate them as new advocates.

Purpose of a success plan
A success plan is the outline and roadmap for achieving customer objectives using tgndata. It is used on an ongoing basis to align on outcomes, action items, and status between the customer and the tgndata team. It is the foundation of a CSM’s engagement with their customers.
The success plan is mutually agreed upon by both sides, ensuring the details are reflective of the customer’s objectives and tgndata’s plan to achieve those objectives and alignment across all involved on those details.
It is a living document, and is reviewed & updated regularly in cadence calls, business reviews, team meetings, and all other situations involving customer journey planning & implementation.
How a success plan is used

section: The success plan is part of most interactions with the customer, and as an ancho
text:
The success plan is part of most interactions with the customer, and as an anchor point for tgndata team planning.
Customer objectives
Customer objectives are at the heart of a success plan. These are the core results that a customer needs to achieve, and define how we will work with the customer to achieve success. An objective has the following elements:
A clearly stated goal & outcome
Measurable success criteria
A timeline to achieve the objective, with steps & action items outlined in initiatives
Owner(s) and stakeholders
These core elements form the foundation for the rest of the success plan and the initiatives that fall under each objective. Using these details, we can determine the steps needed to achieve the objective and track our progress over time.
Initiatives

section: Once an objective has been fully defined, one or more initiatives are created as
text:
Once an objective has been fully defined, one or more initiatives are created as action plans to achieve the objective. These focus on the “how” to meet the customer outcomes, and enable a division of responsibility for different aspects of the plan.
Verifiable Outcomes
Verifiable Outcomes (VOs) are a framework designed to enhance the objectivity and visibility of customer achievements through adoption of tgndata.
Why Verifiable Outcomes?
The purchase of enterprise software only creates meaningful return on investment through careful planning, and dedicated effort over a sustained period of time. To avoid the trap of “no use” it’s crucial that tgndata’s account teams partner with customers to:
Capture the customer’s desired outcomes
Measure and communicate the value of these outcomes in language relevant to the customer
The verifiable outcomes framework has been created to:

section: Drive stakeholder alignment through clear customer-aligned objectives
text:
Drive stakeholder alignment through clear customer-aligned objectives
Capture growth opportunities by clearly illustrating return on investment
Empower strong negotiation positions through evidence-backed discussion of ROI
Improve internal recognition of CS value delivery
What is a Verifiable Outcome?
A verifiable outcome must be SMART:
Specific
Measurable
Attainable
Relevant
Time-bound
To be SMART, outcomes must include:
Baseline metrics: Where we are today
Success criteria: How we’ll know when we’re done
Business impact: The benefit to the customer’s business, in their language
Timeline: When we expect to finish
The Process
Verifiable outcomes progress through a four-stage process, represented by scoped labels applied to objective epics in the success plan:
~Verifiable Outcome::Proposed
Gather baseline metrics
Craft a plan with summary and child initiatives

section: Strategize with account team
text:
Strategize with account team
Present to customer (preferably in a cadence call)
Adjust based on customer feedback
~Verifiable Outcome::Accepted
The customer is aligned on baseline measures, success criteria, and timeline
~Verifiable Outcome::Delivered
Execute on the planned initiatives
Track progress against established metrics
~Verifiable Outcome::Verified
The customer has validated that the desired objective was achieved
Document business impact, in the customer’s words
Best Practices and Guidelines
When developing verifiable outcomes:
Talk to your stakeholders. Ask open-ended “TED” questions.
“Tell me about the most important priorities for your team. How do they relate to broader company objectives?”
“Explain…,” “Describe how…,” etc.
Leverage the resources and examples available to you, including:
Publicly available annual/quarterly investor reports

section: News/Press releases/conference talks and other media
text:
News/Press releases/conference talks and other media
Curate insights from tgndata case studies
Strategize with your account team
Talk to your stakeholders
Examples of Effective and Ineffective Verifiable Outcomes
Imagine you have a customer who wants to achieve faster reaction to competitor moves, detect out-of-stock situations earlier, or save time by automating routine pricing tasks. You agree with their pricing team that, through the use of tgndata’s monitoring, assortment tracking, and automation capabilities, there’s opportunity to standardize workflows, improve data quality, and broaden the use of rules-based pricing decisions.
To bring objectivity and frame the problem in a business-relevant manner, here are three suggested sets of baseline metrics, success criteria, and impact statements.
Baseline Metrics
Success Criteria
Timeframe
Business Impact

It’s unlikely that all three will be relevant to your customer- considering reviewing one or two of your choosing, and align on which measure(s) they feel are most relevant to their situation.
Success plan lifecycle and process
Pre-sales

section: The success plan starts during the pre-sales phase, driven by the sales team. Th
text:
The success plan starts during the pre-sales phase, driven by the sales team. Throughout the product evaluation process they define customer objectives, and use these to demonstrate tgndata value is aligned to these objectives. The sales team documents these objectives in the Account’s success plan with all of the requisite details. This information ensures that we have a clear understanding of the customer’s needed business outcomes.
Post-sales transition

section: Once the sales team closes a customer, the transition to post-sales takes place.
text: Once the sales team closes a customer, the transition to post-sales takes place. The customer goes through onboarding, during which the CSM uses the success plan to outline a plan for adoption and aligns with the customer on the details of this plan. This includes a review of the already-listed objectives (if available) to ensure accuracy and initiatives for each of those objectives related to enablement, implementation, and other actions needed for the customer to achieve their objectives using tgndata.

section: Coming out of this phase, there should be full alignment between the tgndata tea
text:
Coming out of this phase, there should be full alignment between the tgndata team and the customer stakeholders on the objectives and the plan to achieve them, including steps for each of the initiatives, ownership of those steps, and commitment from those owners based on defined timelines. Put simply, everyone should be clear on what comes next and who is responsible/accountable for it.
Enablement and implementation
With the first iteration of the success plan agreed on with the customer, the CSM focuses on putting the plan into action. This has a few key facets:
Overall management of progress against the plan, including regular reviews with stakeholders and initiative owners
Planning and delivery of enablement sessions (workshops, demos, etc.) to the customer in line with the agreed-upon initiatives

section: Recommendations to customer stakeholders on additional areas of opportunity for
text:
Recommendations to customer stakeholders on additional areas of opportunity for adoption and value realization based on existing objectives and knowledge of the customer
The most frequent customer engagement point for this is the cadence call. As the success plan is the hub of our work with the customer, details about initiatives and objectives are incorporated into the cadence call as part of our adoption efforts and overall customer management.
Business reviews
Business reviews, similar to cadence calls, occur on a regular basis and provide the opportunity to review the success plan at a high level and demonstrate progress against the success criteria, as well as discover new objectives for the future.

section: The success plan and business review should be thought of as mirror images of ea
text:
The success plan and business review should be thought of as mirror images of each other: the information maintained in the success plan feeds the discussion for the business review, and new information attained through the business review meeting is captured in the success plan to add to the roadmap for the customer’s success.
Success Plan Components
A success plan consists of two integrated components: the tgndata-based continuous planning project and the Account success plan. These elements work together to ensure ongoing alignment across all stakeholders and enable measurement and analysis of our efforts.
tgndata Continuous Planning Project
The success plan is maintained as a living document within a tgndata Jira project, following our continuous planning methodology. This approach provides several key benefits:
Real-time collaboration and updates through tgndata’s native features

section: Direct integration with daily workflow and project management
text:
Direct integration with daily workflow and project management
Standardized documentation through epic and issue templates
The structure of the success plan in tgndata organizes objectives as epics and initiatives as tasks, with standardized labels and templates ensuring consistent documentation. This makes it easy to track progress, demonstrate measurable results, and maintain up-to-date information that’s accessible to all stakeholders.
For ease of discovery and visibility, the tgndata continuous planning project must be linked in the customer’s Account success plan using the designated field on the plan info screen.
Account Success Plan
Account’s success plan capability makes it easier to share the plan with the customer.

section: While detailed information about objectives and initiatives lives in the tgndata
text:
While detailed information about objectives and initiatives lives in the tgndata project, we maintain key objective actions / updates in the Account’s document timeline.
When an objective is identified and documented as an epic in tgndata, it is also synced to Google Doc. Once an objective is achieved, or if it is removed for any reason, it is closed in both tgndata and Google Doc accordingly.
